topic: What is an automation engineer? Explain what they automate, how tests run, and how to start.
audience: Students and freshers exploring tech careers

scenes.title: The Repetitive Release Check
scenes.narration: Before every release, someone clicks through the same login page and checks the same screens by hand. It is slow, boring, and very easy to get wrong.
scenes.code:
Release checklist
1. Open the login page
2. Enter a test user
3. Check the dashboard
4. Repeat for 50 pages

scenes.title: Turning Steps Into Code
scenes.narration: An automation engineer turns those manual steps into code. This script opens the browser, signs in and checks the result in seconds, every single time.
scenes.code:
def test_login(page):
    page.goto("/login")
    page.fill("#email", "qa@test.in")
    page.click("text=Sign in")
    assert "/home" in page.url

scenes.title: Test Data in JSON
scenes.narration: Test data usually lives in a simple file like this one. The same script can now check an admin and a viewer without changing a single line of code.

scenes.title: Results From the Pipeline
scenes.narration: These tests then run automatically on every code change. The pipeline writes a report like this, so the whole team sees a clear pass or fail.

scenes.title: Skills to Start Today
scenes.narration: To begin, learn Python, one testing tool such as Playwright or Selenium, and the basics of Git and continuous integration. Then automate one boring weekly task.
scenes.code:
skills = [
    "Python basics",
    "Playwright or Selenium",
    "Git and CI pipelines",
]
